ITQAN:v3p266/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p266/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p266/r8.claim: Synonyms can be assigned to distinct locations: وليذكر and أولو الألباب occur apart from Taha's لأولي النهى.
ITQAN:v3p266/r8.anchor: الثامن عشر اختصاص كل من المشتركين بموضع نحو ﴿ وليذكر ﴾ ﴿ أولوا الألباب ﴾

ELMALILI:20:10-54/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:20:10-54/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:20:10-54/r6.claim: Nuhā means reason, which restrains a person from following falsehood and evil.
ELMALILI:20:10-54/r6.anchor: “Nühâ” bâtıla ve fena şeylere uymaktan nehyeden akıl demektir

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r1.claim: These four verses are God's direct insertion, not Moses's speech; the shift makes the past account address present-day Quraysh and identify their true Lord and rightful object of worship and obedience.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r2.claim: The insertion informs Quraysh that the message also concerns them and asks them to recognize who deserves worship and obedience.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r2.anchor: to inform the pharaohs of the Quraysh

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r3.claim: The first two verses point to the being responsible for the created order; its signs reveal providence, wisdom, power, and mercy and support monotheism and judgment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r3.anchor: there are many arguments in them for men of understanding

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r4.claim: Only the one who arranged the earth's provisions deserves to be regarded as Lord; nobody else has a role in them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r4.anchor: only that being is worthy of being regarded as Lord

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p44/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p44/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p44/r1.claim: The first-person wording confirms that the inserted verses are God's words, not part of Moses's conversation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p44/r1.anchor: in the first person and hence they are not part of Moses’ conversation

BURSEVI:v5p304#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p304#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p304#2/r1.claim: The command to eat is an implied speech accompanying God's bringing forth plants, and includes fruits, grains, and similar produce.
BURSEVI:v5p304#2/r1.anchor: {كلوا} حال من ضمير فأخرجنا على إرادة القول أي : أخرجنا منها أصناف النباتات

BURSEVI:v5p304#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p304#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p304#2/r2.claim: Raʿy originally means protecting an animal's life by feeding it or warding off danger; here it means letting livestock graze, with camels, cattle, sheep, and goats named.
BURSEVI:v5p304#2/r2.anchor: {وارعوا} الرعي في الأصل حفظ الحيوان إما بغذائه الحافظ لحياته أو بذب العدو عنه

BURSEVI:v5p304#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p304#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p304#2/r3.claim: People may benefit from livestock directly and indirectly, being permitted to eat some and feed others.
BURSEVI:v5p304#2/r3.anchor: أي اقصدوا بها الانتفاع بالذات وبالواسطة آذنين في الانتفاع بها مبيحين بأن تأكلوا بعضها وتعلفوا بعضها

BURSEVI:v5p304#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p304#2/r4.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p304#2/r4.claim: The Najmiyya reading says the sky, water, plants, livestock, and indeed all creatures were made for human livelihood; without that need God would not have created them.
BURSEVI:v5p304#2/r4.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمية" : يشير إلى أن السماء والماء والنبات والأنعام كلها مخلوقة لكم ولولا احتياجكم للتعيش

BURSEVI:v5p304#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p304#2/r5.speaker: المغربي
BURSEVI:v5p304#2/r5.claim: Al-Maghribī's poem says the whole world exists for the addressee, otherwise that person would not exist in the cosmos.
BURSEVI:v5p304#2/r5.anchor: قال المغربي قدس سره : غرض توبى ز وجود همه جهان ورنه

BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r1.claim: These divine acts are numerous, clear signs of the Creator's oneness, immense power, and wisdom.
BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r1.anchor: المذكور من الشؤون والأفعال الإلهية من جعل الأرض مهدا وسلك السبل فيها وإنزال الماء وإخراج أصناف النبات

BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r2.claim: Ūlū al-nuhā means people of intellect: reason is so named because it restrains falsehood and ugliness, as do the terms ʿaql and ḥijr.
BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r2.anchor: جمع نهية سمي بها العقل لنهيه عن اتباع الباطل وارتكاب القبيح كما سمي بالعقل والحجر لعقله وحجره

BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r3.claim: Although the signs address everyone, the verse singles out people of discerning intellect because they are the ones who benefit from them.
BURSEVI:v5p304#3/r3.anchor: وتخصيص أولي النهى مع أنها آيات للعالمين باعتبار أنهم المنتفعون بها

QASHANI:20:53-55/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:53-55/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:53-55/r3.claim: Eating means nourishing oneself with fitting spiritual states, morals, gifts, and provisions, including contentment, patience, knowledge, perceptions, intentions, and stations.
QASHANI:20:53-55/r3.anchor: اغتذوا وتقووا بما يختص بكم من الأحوال والأخلاق والأمداد والمواهب

QASHANI:20:53-55/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:53-55/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:53-55/r4.claim: Grazing livestock refers to animal faculties and the morals and manners specific to them.
QASHANI:20:53-55/r4.anchor: القوى الحيوانية بما يختص بها من الأخلاق والآداب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r6.claim: After Moses' proof that God is Lord, God continues by recalling His power and unity through creating the earth, paths, rain, plants, and provision.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r6.anchor: ولما ذكر موسى دلالته على ربوبية الله تعالى وتم كلامه عند قوله ولا ينسى ذكر تعالى ما نبه به على قدرته تعالى ووحدانيته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r10.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r10.claim: God's kindness includes providing people with animal fodder from surplus that people cannot eat themselves.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r10.anchor: قالوا: من نعمته عز وجل أن أرزاق العباد إنما تحصل بعمل الأنعام وقد جعل الله علفها مما يفضل عن حاجتهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r11.claim: Eat and pasture are permissive commands, with an implied circumstance: God brings plants forth allowing people to consume some and feed some to livestock.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r11.anchor: كلوا وارعوا أنعامكم أمر إباحة معمول لحال محذوفة أي فأخرجنا قائلين أي آذنين في الانتفاع بها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r12.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r12.claim: Al-Zajjaj notes that raʿā may be intransitive for an animal grazing or transitive for a herder tending and pasturing it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r12.anchor: عدي هنا وارعوا ورعى يكون لازما ومتعديا تقول: رعت الدابة رعيا، ورعاها صاحبها رعاية إذا سامها وسرحها وأراحها قاله الزجاج

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r13.claim: The signs mentioned are God's making the earth a resting place, opening its paths, sending rain, and producing plants.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r13.anchor: وأشار بقوله إن في ذلك للآيات السابقة من جعل الأرض مهدا وسلك سبلها وإنزال الماء وإخراج النبات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r1.claim: Al-nuhā is the plural of nuhya, reason, so named because it restrains people from indecencies; Abu Ali also allows it as a verbal noun like hudā.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r1.anchor: وقالوا النهى جمع نهية وهو العقل سمي بذلك لأنه ينهى عن القبائح

ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r1.claim: An omitted “saying” governs “Eat and graze” as a circumstantial clause for “We brought forth”: plants are prepared for direct human use and indirect use through livestock; the alternative attaches the saying to the plants, but the first is more apt.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r1.anchor: أي أخرجنا اصناف النبات قائلين ( كلوا ) الخ أي

ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj says “رعى” is intransitive of an animal grazing and transitive of its keeper grazing, turning out, and tending it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r2.anchor: ورعى كما قال الزجاج يستعمل لازما ومتعديا يقال : رعت الدابه رعيا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r3.claim: “In that” points to God's acts and affairs; the distant demonstrative can signal their lofty rank and perfection, though another explanation is that its referent is absent.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r3.anchor: إشارة إلى ما ذكر من شؤنه تعالى وافعاله وما فيه من معنى البعد للايذان بعلو رتبته

ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r4.claim: The indefinite “signs” magnifies them in number and quality: they are many, great, and clear proofs of God's attributes and essence.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r4.anchor: للتفخيم كما وكيفا أي لايات كثيرة جليلة واضحة الدلالة على شؤن الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r5.claim: “أولو النهى” means people whose intellect restrains them from falsehood and evil, as “reason” and “ḥijr” also name what restrains.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r5.anchor: جمع نهيه بضم النون سمى بها العقل لنهية عن اتباع الباطل وارتكاب القبيح

ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains “أولي النهى” as people of intellect; another report from him says people of piety, likely an interpretation by implication.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r6.anchor: فانه قال : أي لذوى العقل وفى رواية أخرى عنه أنه قال : لذوى التقى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r7.speaker: أبو علي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r7.claim: Abū ʿAlī permits “النهى” as a verbal noun like “الهدى,” while most commentators take it as a plural for intellects that restrain from falsehood.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r7.anchor: واجاز أبو على أن يكون مصدرا كالهدى والأكثرون على الجمع أي لذوى العقول الناهيه عن الاباطيل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r8.claim: Only rational people recognize the full force of these signs, and God names eating and grazing as their true benefit rather than addressing livestock too.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207#2/r8.anchor: تخصيص كونها آيات بهم لأن اوجه دلالتها على شؤنه تعالى يعلمها إلا العقلاء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278#2/r1.claim: The phrase means to eat and let livestock graze; Arab usage says a person grazes sheep and they graze.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278#2/r1.anchor: {كلوا وارعوا} [أي وارتعوا] (2) {أنعامكم} تقول العرب: رعيت الغنم فرعت

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278#2/r2.claim: People of understanding are called ulul-nuha because nuhya restrains its possessor from indecency and sin.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278#2/r2.anchor: لذوي العقول، واحدتها: "نهية سميت نهية لأنها تنهى صاحبها عن القبائح والمعاصي.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278#2/r3.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278#2/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies people of understanding as those who refrain from what God has forbidden.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278#2/r3.anchor: قال الضحاك: {لأولي النهى} الذين ينتهون عما حرم عليهم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278#2/r4.claim: Qatada says they are people of scrupulous piety.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:54-56/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:54-56/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:54-56/r1.claim: The command to eat and graze livestock is a circumstantial clause with an implied “saying”: the plant kinds were produced for food and fodder, with permission to use them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:54-56/r1.anchor: على إرادة القول أي أخرجنا أصناف النبات قائلين

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:54-56/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:54-56/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:54-56/r2.claim: The signs are for people of reason, whose minds restrain them from falsehood and disgraceful acts; the word is a plural of nahya.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:54-56/r2.anchor: لذوي العقول الناهية عن اتباع الباطل وارتكاب القبائح جمع نهية

BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r4.claim: The commands to eat and pasture livestock reveal careful provision: human food comes through cultivation, while animals eat surplus plants people cannot consume.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r4.anchor: جعل أرزاق العباد بعملها تنعيما لهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r5.claim: The world's provisions meet every creature's needs across changing conditions, for their journey to God and presentation before Him; this completeness proves God does not err or forget.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r5.anchor: أبدع هذا العالم شاملا لكل ما يحتاجه من فيه لما خلقهم له من السفر إليه والعرض عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r6.claim: Unlike God, a human maker eventually discovers defects in a product and must repeatedly work to remove them.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r6.anchor: لو عمل شيئا واجتهد كل الاجتهاد في تكميله

BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r7.claim: The signs are for minds that restrain their owners from wrongdoing; those blind to them have no effective reason, since useless reason is as if absent. The point is emphasized because deniers reject it.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r7.anchor: العقول التي من شأنها أن تنهى صاحبها عن الغي

BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r8.speaker: ابن إسحاق
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r8.claim: Ibn Kathir cites a poem that Ibn Ishaq attributes in the Sira to Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r8.anchor: عزاه ابن اسحاق في السيرة لزيد بن عمرو بن نفيل

BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r9.speaker: ابن هشام
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r9.claim: Ibn Hisham instead attributes the cited poem to Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r9.anchor: وابن هشام لأمية بن أبي الصلت

BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r10.claim: The cited poem challenges Pharaoh to claim that he made earth without supports, raised the sky without pillars, set its light, brings the sun, and grows crops and grain.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r10.anchor: فقولا له آأنت سويت هذه بلا وتد حتى استقلت كما هيا

DURR-FULL:v5p582/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r11.claim: He glosses those endowed with understanding as people of piety.
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r11.anchor: وفي قوله: {لأولي النهى} قال: لأولي التقى

DURR-FULL:v5p582/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r12.claim: He also glosses those endowed with understanding as people of intelligence and sound judgment.
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r12.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {لأولي النهى} قال: لذوي الحجا والعقول

DURR-FULL:v5p582/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r13.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r13.claim: He explains the people of understanding as people of scrupulous restraint.
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r13.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {لأولي النهى} قال: لأولي الورع

DURR-FULL:v5p582/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r14.speaker: سفيان
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r14.claim: He defines them as those who refrain from what they have been forbidden.
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r14.anchor: عن سفيان رضي الله عنه في قوله: {لأولي النهى} قال: الذين ينتهون عما نهوا عنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p239/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p239/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p239/r1.claim: Shatta is the plural of shatīt, meaning scattered or diverse; here it refers to differing forms, colors, and tastes, some suitable for people and others for animals.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p239/r1.anchor: وشتى : جمع شتيت بوزن فعلى ، مثل : مريض ومرضى . والشتيت : المشتت ، أي المبعد . وأريد به هنا التباعد في الصفات من الشكل واللون والطعم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p239/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p239/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p239/r2.claim: Eat and graze your cattle is reported speech with an omitted saying; the commands permit use as a blessing, implicitly from the plants, and distribute different foods among people and livestock.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p239/r2.anchor: والجملة الثانية { كلوا وارعوا أنعامكم } مقول قول محذوف هو حال من ضمير { فأخرجنا . والتقدير : قائلين : كلوا وارعوا أنعامكم . والأمر للإباحة مراد به المنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p239/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p239/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p239/r3.claim: Raʿā is both intransitive and transitive, with infinitives الرعي and الرعاية respectively; al-Nabigha's line uses the transitive sense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p239/r3.anchor: وفعل ( رعى ) يستعمل قاصرا ومتعديا . يقال : رعت الدابة ورعاها صاحبها . وفرق بينهما في المصدر فمصدر القاصر : الرعي ، ومصدر المتعدي : الرعاية . ومنه قول النابغة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p239/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p239/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p239/r4.claim: The concluding sentence is an inserted reinforcement: it gathers the many signs in creation that point to the Creator's existence and oneness and attest to His blessing for reflective people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p239/r4.anchor: والجملة الثالثة إن في ذالك لآيات لأولى النهى } معترضة مؤكدة للاستدلال ؛ فبعد أن أشير إلى ما في المخلوقات المذكورة آنفا من الدلالة على وجود الصانع ووحدانيته ، والمنة بها على الإنسان لمن تأمل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p239/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p239/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p239/r5.claim: The particle inna emphasizes the claim because the audience behaves as if denying the signs despite thinking itself wise; reflection and reminders would reveal their many indications.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p239/r5.anchor: وتأكيد الخبر بحرف ( إن ) لتنزيل المخاطبين منزلة المنكرين ، لأنهم لم ينظروا في دلالة تلك المخلوقات على وحدانية الله ، وهم يحسبون أنفسهم من أولي النهى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p239/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p239/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p239/r6.claim: Nuhā is a collective noun for reason; it is so called because reason restrains its possessor from corrupting and destructive acts, like the terms ʿaql and ḥijr.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p239/r6.anchor: والنهى : اسم جمع نهية بضم النون وسكون الهاء ، أي العقل ، سمي نهية لأنه سبب انتهاء المتحلي به عن كثير من الأعمال المفسدة والمهلكة ، ولذلك أيضا سمي بالعقل وسمي بالحجر .

FARRA:v2p180/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p180/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p180/r7.claim: The signs for people of understanding lie in the plants’ differing colors and tastes; ذو نهية means a person of intellect.
FARRA:v2p180/r7.anchor: يقول: في اختلاف ألوانه وطعمه آيات لذوي العقول

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p279#7/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p279#7/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p279#7/r1.claim: Al-nuhā means intellects, and nahya means reason; Dhū al-Rumma's poetic phrase dhī nihya describes a person of understanding.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p279#7/r1.anchor: لذي نهية إلا إلى أم سالم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r7.claim: Eat and graze means the plants are fit for people to eat and for livestock to graze; the imperative uses the most desirable and calming actions.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r7.anchor: وقوله كلوا وارعوا بمعنى هي صالحة لأن يؤكل منها وترعى الغنم فيها فأخرج العبارة في صيغة الأمر لأنه أرجى الأفعال وأهدأها للنفوس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r8.claim: Al-nuhā is the plural of nuhya, the intellect that restrains from disgraceful acts.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r8.anchor: والنهى جمع نهية والنهية العقل الناهي عن القبائح

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p293/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p293/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p293/r1.claim: The command means to eat the fruits God produced and let livestock graze; the verb raʿā describes turning animals loose in pasture.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p293/r1.anchor: كلوا أي مما أخرجنا لكم من الثمار وارعوا أنعامكم يقال رعى الماشية يرعاها إذا سرحها في المرعى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p293/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p293/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p293/r2.claim: These commands remind people of God’s blessings.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p293/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p293/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p293/r3.claim: The signs are lessons in the variety of plants’ colors and tastes.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p293/r3.anchor: إن في ذلك لآيات أي لعبرا في اختلاف الألوان والطعوم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p293/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p293/r4.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p293/r4.claim: Al-Farraʾ glosses ūlī al-nuhā as people of understanding.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p293/r4.anchor: قال الفراء لذوي العقول يقال للرجل إنه لذو نهية إذا كان ذا عقل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p293/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p293/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p293/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj says nuhya is the singular of nuhā: the intellect that restrains from wrong and leads to good; another linguistic view calls it a person guided by his own judgment, which he also approves.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p293/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج واحد النهى نهية يقال فلان ذو نهية أي ذو عقل ينتهي به عن المقابح ويدخل به في المحاسن قال وقال بعض أهل اللغة ذو النهية الذي ينتهى إلى رأيه وعقله وهذا حسن أيضا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p299/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p299/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p299/r1.claim: The earth's signs are proofs for sound-minded people that God alone is deity and Lord.

JISHUMI:v7p4676/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4676/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4676/r8.claim: Ulū al-nuhā are people of intellect; the word derives from restraining the self from ugliness or from people reaching their judgment.
JISHUMI:v7p4676/r8.anchor: وسموا أولي النهى؛ لأنهم ينهون النفس عن القبائح، وقيل: لأنه ينتهى إلى رأيهم.

JISHUMI:v7p4676/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4676/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4676/r9.claim: The verb raʿā may be intransitive or transitive.
JISHUMI:v7p4676/r9.anchor: يقال: رعيت الغنم فرعت لازم ومتعد.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r15.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r15.claim: “Eat and pasture” describes God's bringing forth vegetation with permission to eat some and feed some to livestock.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r15.anchor: المعنى : أخرجنا أصناف النبات آذنين في الانتفاع بها

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p407/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p407/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p407/r1.claim: Al-nuhā can mean people of judgment, intellect, or scrupulous restraint.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p407/r1.anchor: لأولي النهى } فيه ثلاثة أوجه : أحدها : أولي الحكم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p407/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p407/r2.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p407/r2.claim: Al-nuhā means people endowed with intellect.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p407/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p407/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p407/r3.claim: Al-nuhā can also mean people of piety and scrupulousness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p407/r3.anchor: الثالث : أولي الورع . وفي تسميتهم بذلك

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p407/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p407/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p407/r4.claim: They are called al-nuhā because they restrain the self from reprehensible conduct.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p407/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p407/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p407/r5.claim: They may be called al-nuhā because judgment ultimately rests with their opinions.

MUQATIL:20:54-56/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:54-56/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:54-56/r1.claim: Eating and grazing livestock among the described signs gives people of reason a lesson in God's oneness; Moses says this to Pharaoh.
MUQATIL:20:54-56/r1.anchor: { كلوا وارعوا أنعامكم إن في ذلك } يعنى فيما ذكر من هذه الآية { لآيات } يعنى لعبرة { لأولي النهى }

NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#6/r1.claim: The permission to eat and pasture animals is a circumstantial clause attached to God’s bringing forth plants: He produced kinds of vegetation while allowing some to be eaten and some used as fodder.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#6/r1.anchor: حال من الضمير في فأخرجنا والمعنى أخرجنا اصناف النبات آذنين في الانتفاع بها مبيحين أن تأكلوا بعضها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#6/r2.claim: The things mentioned are signs, meaning indications.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#6/r2.anchor: ﴿ إن في ذلك ﴾ في الذي ذكرت ﴿ لآيات ﴾ لدلالات

NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#6/r3.claim: Ulū al-nuhā are people of reason; nuhya is singular because reason restrains from forbidden acts or serves as the endpoint consulted in affairs.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#6/r3.anchor: لذوي العقول واحدها نهية تنهى عن المحظور أو ينتهى اليها في الامور

QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r13.claim: “Eat and graze your cattle” is a command granting permission.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r13.anchor: قوله تعالى: { كلوا وارعوا أنعامكم } أمر إباحة.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r14.claim: Raʿā can describe the livestock grazing, while the owner pastures or sends them out; the verb is both intransitive and transitive.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r14.anchor: { وارعوا } من رعت الماشية الكلأ، ورعاها صاحبها رعاية أي أسامها وسرحها لازم ومتعد

QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r15.claim: Ulū al-nuhā means people of intellect; its singular is nuhya because judgment returns to them, or because they restrain themselves from indecencies.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r15.anchor: أي العقول. الواحدة نهية. قال لهم ذلك لأنهم الذين ينتهى إلى رأيهم. وقيل: لأنهم ينهون النفس عن القبائح.

RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r8.claim: Razi insists it must be a predicate of an omitted subject; the other parses make it Moses’ speech, conflicting with the later shift to “We brought forth.”
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r8.anchor: إذ لو حملناه على الوجهين الباقيين لزم كونه من كلام موسى عليه السلام ولو كان كذلك لفسد النظم بسبب قوله : { فأخرجنا به أزواجا

RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r6.claim: Eat and graze is a circumstantial clause attached to the pronoun in We brought forth: the plants were produced with permission to use some for food and some for fodder.
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r6.anchor: فهو حال من الضمير في أخرجنا والمعنى أخرجنا أصناف النبات آذنين في الانتفاع بها مبيحين أن تأكلوا بعضها وتعلفوا بعضها

RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r7.claim: The command to eat encompasses all beneficial uses; Razi compares the idiom with Qur’anic expressions about consuming wealth.
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r7.anchor: وقد تضمن قوله كلوا سائر وجوه المنافع فهو كقوله : { ولا تأكلوا أموالكم بينكم بالباطل }

RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r8.claim: Eat is a command of permission, and the blessings just described are signs for people of sound reason; nuhā means intellect.
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r8.anchor: وقوله : { كلوا } أمر إباحة { إن فى ذلك } أي فيما ذكرت من هذه النعم { لايات } أي لدلالات لذوي النهى أي العقول

RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r9.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r9.claim: Abu Ali al-Farisi says nuhā may be a verbal noun like hudā or a plural form.
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r9.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي : النهي يجوز أن يكون مصدرا كالهدى ويجوز أن يكون جمعا

STUDYQURAN:20:53/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:53/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:53/r2.claim: The commentary points to the benefits of cattle discussed in other verses.
STUDYQURAN:20:53/r2.anchor: For the benefits of cattle, see 6:142c; 16:5–7c.

STUDYQURAN:20:53/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:53/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:53/r3.claim: Nuhā derives from a root also meaning restraint or prohibition; here it describes rational people who avoid vile acts and thoughts.
STUDYQURAN:20:53/r3.anchor: nuhā, which is derived from a root that also connotes “restraining” or “prohibiting”; here it refers to those who, through the use of their rational faculties

SAMIN-DURR:20:54/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:54/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:54/r1.claim: كلوا is governed by an omitted قول that is circumstantial to the subject of أخرجنا: God brought out the plants while saying “eat.”
SAMIN-DURR:20:54/r1.anchor: قوله: { كلوا }: منصوب بقول محذوف، وذلك القول منصوب على الحال من فاعل " أخرجنا " تقديره: فأخرجنا كذا قائلين: كلوا.

SAMIN-DURR:20:54/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:54/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:54/r2.claim: The object of eating is omitted, as in 2:60.
SAMIN-DURR:20:54/r2.anchor: وترك مفعول الأكل على حد تركه في قوله تعالى:

SAMIN-DURR:20:54/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:54/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:54/r3.claim: رعى can be transitive or intransitive; it is transitive in this verse.
SAMIN-DURR:20:54/r3.anchor: ورعت الدابة ترعى رعيا فيه راعية، وجاء في الآية متعديا.

SAMIN-DURR:20:54/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:54/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:54/r4.claim: النُّهى is either the plural of نُهية, or a singular verbal noun like الهدى and السرى, as Abū ʿAlī says.
SAMIN-DURR:20:54/r4.anchor: والنهى فيه قولان، أحدهما: أنه جمع نهية كغرف جمع غرفة. والثاني: أنها اسم مفرد وهو مصدر كالهدى والسرى. قاله أبو علي.

SAMIN-DURR:20:54/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:54/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:54/r5.claim: النُّهى means intellect; it is so named because it restrains its possessor from shameful acts, and this weak-final verbal noun is an unusual fifth example.
SAMIN-DURR:20:54/r5.anchor: والنهى: العقل. قالوا: سمي بذلك لأنه ينهى صاحبه عن ارتكاب القبائح.

TAB-FULL:v16p86#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p86#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p86#2/r1.claim: Al-Tabari says the plants provide provisions for the people's livestock to graze.

TAB-FULL:v16p86#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p86#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p86#2/r2.claim: These provisions display God's power and sovereignty and point to His oneness and the fact that He alone is God.
TAB-FULL:v16p86#2/r2.anchor: من قدرة ربكم، وعظيم سلطانه لآيات: يعني لدلالات وعلامات تدل على وحدانية ربكم

TAB-FULL:v16p86#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p86#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p86#2/r3.claim: The people of reason are singled out because they reflect, learn from signs, and take admonition; nuhā is the plural of nuhya.
TAB-FULL:v16p86#2/r3.anchor: {أولي النهى} يعني: أهل الحجى والعقول. والنهى: جمع نهية

TAB-FULL:v16p206#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p206#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p206#2/r1.claim: Tabari explains the signs through earlier divine punishment and says the transmitted exegetes agree with his account.
TAB-FULL:v16p206#2/r1.anchor: وبنحو الذي قلنا في ذلك قال أهل التأويل

TAB-FULL:v16p206#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p206#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p206#2/r2.claim: Those possessing understanding and reason, whose intellect, comprehension, and religion restrain them from harmful conduct, are the people meant by ulū al-nuhā.
TAB-FULL:v16p206#2/r2.anchor: ودينه عن مواقعة ما يضره. وبنحو الذي

TAB-FULL:v16p206#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p206#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p206#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses ulū al-nuhā as the pious.
TAB-FULL:v16p206#2/r3.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، قوله: {لأولي النهى} [طه: 54] يقول: التقى

TAB-FULL:v16p206#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p206#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p206#2/r4.claim: Qatada glosses the people of understanding as people of scrupulous piety.
TAB-FULL:v16p206#2/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، {إن في ذلك لآيات لأولي النهى} [طه: 54] أهل الورع

TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r6.claim: 'Nuhay' is the plural of 'nahya,' meaning intellect, so called because it restrains a person from following desire.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r6.anchor: النهى جمع نهية بالضم فالسكون وهو العقل سمي به لنهيه عن اتباع الهوى

ZAJJAJ:v3p359/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p359/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p359/r1.claim: Ūlū al-nuhā means people of reason; nuhya is its singular, and reason restrains its possessor from shameful acts and leads to good.
ZAJJAJ:v3p359/r1.anchor: يقال: فلان ذو نهية ومعناه ذو عقل ينتهي به عن المقابح

ZAJJAJ:v3p359/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p359/r2.speaker: بعض أهل اللغة
ZAJJAJ:v3p359/r2.claim: Some linguists say a person of nuhya follows the judgment and reason he has reached; the author also considers this sound.
ZAJJAJ:v3p359/r2.anchor: وقال بعض أهل اللغة: ذو النهية الذي ينتهى إلى رأيه وعقله.

TABRISI:20:52-53/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:52-53/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:52-53/r8.claim: Nuhā is the plural of nuhyah; people of reason are called that because they restrain others from indecencies.
TABRISI:20:52-53/r8.anchor: والنهي جمع نهية وإنما قيل لأولي العقول أولو النهى

TABRISI:20:52-53/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:52-53/r9.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:20:52-53/r9.claim: Another explanation says people of reason are so called because others defer to their judgments.

TABRISI:20:53-56/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:53-56/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:53-56/r4.claim: The command to eat from the rain-produced plants and fruits and pasture livestock is phrased as an order but means permission and a reminder of God's favor.
TABRISI:20:53-56/r4.anchor: واللفظ للأمر والمراد الإباحة والتذكير بالنعمة

TABRISI:20:53-56/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:53-56/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TABRISI:20:53-56/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk interprets people of intellect as those who restrain themselves from what God has forbidden.
TABRISI:20:53-56/r5.anchor: الذين ينتهون عما حرم الله عليهم عن الضحاك

TABRISI:20:53-56/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:53-56/r6.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:20:53-56/r6.claim: Qatādah interprets people of intellect as people of scrupulous piety.

TABRISI:20:53-56/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:53-56/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:20:53-56/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets them as people of piety.

THALABI:v6p247#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p247#2/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p247#2/r4.claim: Eat and pasture means eat and let the livestock graze; Arabic uses raʿaytu al-ghanam both transitively and intransitively.
THALABI:v6p247#2/r4.anchor: ثم قال كلوا وارعوا أي ارتعوا أنعامكم يقول العرب: رعيت الغنم فرعت لازم ومتعد.

THALABI:v6p247#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p247#2/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p247#2/r5.claim: Ulū al-nuhā means people of reason, called that because reason restrains its possessor from shameful and forbidden acts.
THALABI:v6p247#2/r5.anchor: لأولي النهى أي لذوي العقول، واحدها نهية، سميت بذلك لأنها تنهى صاحبها عن القبائح والفضائح وارتكاب المحظورات والمحرمات.

THALABI:v6p247#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p247#2/r6.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v6p247#2/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets the people of reason as those who refrain from what God has forbidden.
THALABI:v6p247#2/r6.anchor: وقال الضحاك: لأولي النهى يعني الذين ينتهون عما حرم عليهم.

THALABI:v6p247#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p247#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v6p247#2/r7.claim: Qatada glosses them as people of piety and scrupulousness.

THALABI:v6p247#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p247#2/r8.speaker: علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p247#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ali ibn Abi Talha, glosses them as people of taqwa.
THALABI:v6p247#2/r8.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس: لذوي التقى.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r1.claim: ‘Eat and graze’ refers to the plants produced by the rain.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {كلوا وارعوا} أي: مما أخرجنا بالمطر من النبات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r2.claim: The flock itself grazes the pasture; its owner tends it by letting it graze, turning it out, and bringing it back.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r2.anchor: يقال: رعت الماشية الكلأ رعيا، ورعاها صاحبها رعاية، إذا أسامها وسرحها وأراحها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r3.claim: The command permits grazing livestock in the rain-grown pasture and reminds people of God’s blessing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r3.anchor: والمعنى: أسيموا مواشيكم فيما أنبتناه بالمطر، وهذا أمر إباحة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas connects this reminder to 80:27–32, where God grows grain and other provisions for people and livestock.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هذا كقوله: {فأنبتنا فيها حبا} -إلى قوله- {متاعا لكم ولأنعامكم}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r5.claim: The signs in the rain and plants point to God’s oneness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r5.anchor: معنى ما ذكر من الدلالة على توحيده

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r6.speaker: اللحياني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r6.claim: Al-Lihyani says nuhā means intellect and derives the name from the mind stopping at what it is commanded and not overstepping.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r6.anchor: قال اللحياني: (النهية: العقل، والنهى جمع نهيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r7.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r7.claim: Abu Ishaq says a person of nuhya has reason that restrains vice and leads to good, or follows the judgment of reason; he considers the latter explanation better.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r7.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: (يقال: فلان ذو نهية، ومعناه ذو عقل ينتهي به عن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r8.claim: The two etymologies converge: intellect restrains a person from reprehensible acts.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r8.anchor: وقد رجع القولان في اشتقاق النهية إلى قول واحد، وهو الحبس، والنهية هي التي تنهي وتحبس عن المقابح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r9.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r9.claim: Abu Ali says nuhā may be a verbal noun like hudā or a plural like ẓulum; the plural reading is supported by its addition to ‘possessors,’ though a singular verbal noun can stand for a plural.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r9.anchor: قال أبو علي: (لا يخلو النهى من أن يكون مصدرا كالهدى، أو جمعا كالظلم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r10.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r10.claim: Abu Ali derives nuhā from restraint or confinement, like a place where water is held; the author says this too returns to the mind’s restraining function.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r10.anchor: والنهى معناه في اللغة: الثبات والحبس، ومنه النهى والتنهية للمكان الذي ينتهي إليه الماء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r11.claim: In ʿAta’s narration, Ibn Abbas says the signs are a lesson for people of understanding who restrain themselves from disobeying God; al-Dahhak gives a similar explanation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: ({لآيات لأولي النهى} يريد العبرة لذوي العقول)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p422/r12.claim: In al-Walibi’s narration, Ibn Abbas glosses ‘possessors of insight’ as the pious.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:51-54/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:51-54/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:51-54/r6.claim: People may eat the plants and pasture their livestock by letting them graze in the earth's vegetation; this is a lesson for people of reason.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:51-54/r6.anchor: إن في ذلك } الذي ذكرت { لآيات } لعبرة { لأولي النهي } لذوي العقول

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r5.claim: People are to eat and let their livestock graze on the plants just described.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r5.anchor: قوله: {كلوا وارعوا أنعامكم} [طه: 54] من ذلك النبات.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r6.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r6.claim: Qatada says the people of discernment are those marked by piety.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r6.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة قال: لأولي الورع.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r7.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says the people of discernment are people of intellect.
